questions.text: This is a 120 mm tall, thin-walled column (typical section ≈ 2 mm, no overhangs, no bridges). Its shape doesn't reveal what it's for. What is it for?

options.label: Display / lightweight
options.impact: All preset values; light and quick to print. The 2-wall shell (≈0.84 mm) plus 15% zig-zag is adequate for a part that won't carry load.
options.why: The part's features give no reason to deviate: no overhang, no bridge, slenderness under the brim threshold, bed contact well above 200 mm². Per the Sponsor's practice, the preset stands unless the part or its purpose provides a reason. Without a stated load or visible surface, it doesn't.

options.label: Structural / load-bearing
options.impact: 3 walls (≈1.26 mm) in a ~2 mm section leaves ~0.7 mm for infill; grid lines will be thin and Orca may merge some. Noticeably stiffer against bending and crushing, but print time increases.
options.why: Would be the right call if this column carries a shelf or resists lateral force, but the part's geometry alone doesn't show that.

options.label: Visible top surface
options.impact: The 2825 mm² flat top gets 1.4 mm of solid layers instead of 1.0 mm; smoother, less layer-line visible. Marginally longer print; walls and infill unchanged.
options.why: Matters only if the top face is a finished surface (e.g., the top of a vase, a lamp shade, or a display base). The shape doesn't confirm that.
